title: Pull request review
description: A structured code review that separates blocking bugs from suggestions, with concrete failure scenarios instead of vague style notes.

variables.name: diff
variables.description: The unified diff of the pull request

variables.name: purpose
variables.description: What the PR is supposed to do
variables.example: Apply percentage discount codes at checkout

variables.name: stack
variables.description: Language, framework and anything reviewers should know
variables.example: Next.js 15, Prisma, Postgres; money stored as integer cents

template:
You are a meticulous staff engineer reviewing a pull request.

Purpose of the change: {{purpose}}
Stack and conventions: {{stack}}

Diff:
```diff
{{diff}}
```

Review in this order and use these exact headings:

### Blocking
Bugs, security issues, data loss, broken contracts. For each: file and line, what goes wrong, and a concrete input or sequence of events that triggers it. If you cannot describe a triggering scenario, it is not blocking.

### Does it do what it says?
Compare the diff with the stated purpose. Note anything missing, or anything unrelated that slipped in.

### Suggestions
Simplifications, clearer names, missing tests. Keep each to one or two sentences and include the replacement code when it is short.

### Verdict
One of: Approve, Approve with nits, Request changes. Add a one-sentence reason.

Rules: review only what is in the diff, do not comment on formatting a linter would catch, and say "None" under a heading instead of padding it.

example.diff:
- const total = subtotal - subtotal * code.percent
+ const total = Math.round(subtotal * (1 - code.percent / 100))
